parts.latex:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic series is given by $S_n=2n(n+2)$.

Find the first term and the common difference of the series.

solutions.latex:
$S_n=2n(n+2)$
$$\begin{aligned}\therefore\ T_1&=S_1=6\\ T_2&=S_2-S_1\\ &=16-6\\ &=10\end{aligned}$$
Hence the common difference is $T_2-T_1=4$.
criteria: Substantial progress, e.g. finds the first term

meta.top_criterion_original: Finds value of first two terms and hence the common difference

parts.latex:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic sequence is $S_n=3n^2-4n$, where $n>1$.

Find the $n$th term, $T_n$, \underline{\textbf{and}} state the common difference.

meta.top_criterion_original: Marks not itemised on the copy (3 marks): use of $T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$; $T_n=6n-7$; $d=6$
meta.rubric_note: Source gives 3 marks without itemising them (use of T_n = S_n - S_(n-1); T_n = 6n - 7; d = 6); written top-down in that order.

solutions.latex:
Write each term as a multiple of $\ln 3$:

$$\begin{aligned} \sum_{n=4}^{n}\ln 3^{2n} &= \ln 3^8+\ln 3^{10}+\ln 3^{12}+\ldots+\ln 3^{2n} \\ &= 8\ln 3+10\ln 3+12\ln 3+\ldots+2n\ln 3 \\ &= \ln 3\,(8+10+12+\ldots+2n) \end{aligned}$$

The bracket is an arithmetic series with $a=8$, $d=2$ and last term $l=2n$.

Running from $4$ to $n$, it has $n-3$ terms, and the sum is $\dfrac{\text{number of terms}}{2}(a+l)$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Sum} &= \ln 3\left[\dfrac{n-3}{2}(8+2n)\right] \\ &= \ln 3\left[\dfrac{n-3}{2}\cdot 2(4+n)\right] \\ &= (n-3)(n+4)\ln 3 \end{aligned}$$

Rationalise the denominator.
$$\begin{aligned} \sum_{r=1}^{63}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r+1}+\sqrt{r}} &= \sum_{r=1}^{63}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r+1}+\sqrt{r}}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}}{\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}}\right) \\ &= \sum_{r=1}^{63}\left(\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}\right) \end{aligned}$$
The terms telescope.
$$\begin{aligned} \sum_{r=1}^{63}\left(\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}\right) &= (\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1})+(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})+\cdots+(\sqrt{63}-\sqrt{62})+(\sqrt{64}-\sqrt{63}) \\ &= -1+\sqrt{64} \\ &= 7 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Rationalises the denominator, or equivalent merit

1761.stem: The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic series is given by $S_n=\dfrac{1}{2}n(3n+2)$.

parts.latex: Find the first three terms of the series.
Find an expression for the $n$th term of the series.

solutions.latex:
The first term is $T_1=S_1$, and each later term is $T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$ (the sum of $n$ terms less the sum of $n-1$ terms).
$$\begin{aligned} S_1 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(1)\big(3(1)+2\big)=\dfrac{5}{2} \\ S_2 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(2)\big(3(2)+2\big)=8 \\ S_3 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(3)\big(3(3)+2\big)=\dfrac{33}{2} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} T_1 &= S_1=\dfrac{5}{2} \\ T_2 &= S_2-S_1=8-\dfrac{5}{2}=\dfrac{11}{2} \\ T_3 &= S_3-S_2=\dfrac{33}{2}-8=\dfrac{17}{2} \end{aligned}$$
The first three terms are $\dfrac{5}{2}$, $\dfrac{11}{2}$ and $\dfrac{17}{2}$.

From part (a), $a=\dfrac{5}{2}$ and $d=\dfrac{11}{2}-\dfrac{5}{2}=3$. Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned} T_n &= \dfrac{5}{2}+(n-1)\cdot 3 \\ &= \dfrac{5}{2}+3n-3 \\ &= 3n-\dfrac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, using $T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned} T_n &= \dfrac{1}{2}n(3n+2)-\dfrac{1}{2}(n-1)\big(3(n-1)+2\big) \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big[3n^2+2n-(n-1)(3n-1)\big] \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big[3n^2+2n-(3n^2-4n+1)\big] \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}(6n-1) \\ &= 3n-\dfrac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic series is given by the formula

$S_n=3n^2-17n$, where $n>0$. Find an expression for the $n$th term of the series.

solutions.latex:
For any series, the $n$th term is the difference of consecutive sums, $T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$.
$$\begin{aligned}T_n&=S_n-S_{n-1}\\&=3n^2-17n-\left[3(n-1)^2-17(n-1)\right]\\&=3n^2-17n-3\left(n^2-2n+1\right)+17n-17\\&=3n^2-17n-3n^2+6n-3+17n-17\\&=6n-20\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ T_n=6n-20$$

meta.format_note: Rubric was one mark per step; rewritten top-down. Checked: T_1=S_1=-14=6-20.

2333.stem: The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic series is given by $S_n=25n-2n^2$.

parts.latex: Show that the general term is given by $T_n=27-4n$.

solutions.latex:
The first term is $T_1=S_1$.
$$\begin{aligned}S_1&=25(1)-2(1)^2\\&=23\end{aligned}$$
So the first term is $23$.

Find the first three terms from the sums, using $T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$.
$$\begin{aligned}T_1&=23\\S_2&=25(2)-2(2)^2=42,&T_2&=S_2-S_1=19\\S_3&=25(3)-2(3)^2=57,&T_3&=S_3-S_2=15\end{aligned}$$
The terms are $23,\ 19,\ 15,\ \ldots$
$$d=19-23=-4$$

meta.format_note: Rubric rows kept from the source (2: Correct solution, 1: finding correctly the 2nd term).

parts.latex: For the arithmetic series defined by $S_n = 2n^2 + 3n$, find the first, second and tenth terms.

solutions.latex:
The first term equals the first sum.
$$\begin{aligned} T_1 &= S_1 \\ &= 2(1)^2 + 3(1) \\ &= 5 \end{aligned}$$
Using $S_2 = T_1 + T_2$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_2 &= 2(2)^2 + 3(2) = 14 \\ 14 &= 5 + T_2 \\ T_2 &= 9 \end{aligned}$$
So $a=5$ and $d=9-5=4$.
$$\begin{aligned} T_{10} &= a + 9d \\ &= 5 + 9\times 4 \\ &= 41 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ T_1 = 5,\ T_2 = 9,\ T_{10} = 41$$
criteria: Finds two of the three terms, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A sequence is defined by the recurrence relation

$$u_{n+1} = 0.3u_n + 6 \text{ with } u_{10} = 10.$$

What is the value of $u_{12}$ ?

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} u_{11} &= 0.3\times u_{10} + 6 \\ &= 0.3\times 10 + 6 \\ &= 9 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} u_{12} &= 0.3\times u_{11} + 6 \\ &= 0.3\times 9 + 6 \\ &= 8.7 \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

parts.latex: The $n^{\text{th}}$ term of a series is given by $T_n=2n^2-4$ for $n\ge 1$. What is the sum of the first three terms?

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} T_1&=2(1)^2-4=-2 \\ T_2&=2(2)^2-4=4 \\ T_3&=2(3)^2-4=14 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Sum}&=-2+4+14 \\ &=16 \end{aligned}$$
This matches option D.
